edges.description: Profound deficiency of active thyroid hormones impairs cellular thermogenesis and basal metabolic heat production, resulting in core hypothermia.
Severe thyroid hormone deficiency slows skeletal muscle relaxation and peripheral neuromuscular conduction, producing delayed deep tendon reflexes.
Profound hypothyroidism reduces gastrointestinal smooth muscle motility, causing constipation, gastric atony, and paralytic ileus.
Low cardiac output and hypovolemia stimulate ADH release, impairing free water excretion.
Respiratory decompensation can progress through hypercarbia and CNS depression to coma.
Cardiovascular depression in myxedema coma includes bradycardia.
Cardiovascular involvement in myxedema coma includes pericardial fluid accumulation.
Reduced ventilatory drive produces hypoventilation with hypercarbia.
In-hospital hypotension is part of the severe decompensated presentation and predicts mortality.
ADH-mediated water retention contributes directly to low sodium in myxedema coma.
Cutaneous myxedema produces non-pitting edema of the face, hands, and feet.
Cutaneous involvement includes dry, scaly skin.
Tissue edema in myxedema can include macroglossia.
Hair thinning or sparse body hair is part of the skin and appendage involvement in myxedema coma.
Superimposed infection and pneumonia accelerate respiratory depression, hypercarbia, and systemic decompensation in severely hypothyroid patients.
Severe environmental cold overwhelms impaired hypothyroid thermogenesis and precipitates systemic decompensation into myxedema coma.
Sedatives, analgesics, hypnotics, and anesthetics suppress ventilatory drive, precipitating respiratory decompensation and myxedema coma.
